propositions: rebar's LLM runtime lacks first-class Bedrock support and routes all AWS-hosted Claude through OpenAI-compatible gateways, losing prompt caching, retrying transport, read timeout, and native structured output

provider behavior is selected by string prefix matching on resolved model names rather than through a pluggable provider factory, violating provider abstraction and creating undocumented capability gaps
configuration keys REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY are documented as working but rejected at runtime by _pai_check_config, making the documentation false

signed verdict sidecars record a model string that no longer names the provider that answered when routed through proxies, eliminating provenance and preventing attestation consumers from distinguishing first-class from best-effort results

capability detection (output modes, prompt caching, thinking support) is hardcoded to provider-name string sets rather than derived from pydantic-ai's ModelProfile, making the capability table fragile and provider-dependent code scattered across multiple modules

Bedrock's retry, timeout, and cache configuration do not route through LLMConfig fields and remain unconfigured in the live path, creating asymmetry between first-class and best-effort providers and leaving production unprotected against transient failures
